summary: Postinstall host reconnaissance and environment exfiltration to webhook.site
details: The package's postinstall script (install.js, wired via package.json "postinstall": "node install.js") executes a battery of host reconnaissance commands on install — id, hostname, uname -a, env, ps aux, cat /etc/passwd, listing of /home, ip addr, ss -tulpn — and POSTs the collected output as JSON via https.request to a hardcoded webhook.site capture endpoint (https://webhook.site/cfe35ac2-bec3-48b8-bae1-a49dea5412c2). The full `env` dump routinely contains CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, and registry tokens (AWS_*, NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.), which are shipped off-host along with account and network state. The package's stated purpose (a Chrome DevTools debug proxy) has no need to read /etc/passwd or ship environment variables to an anonymous webhook. Execution fires automatically on `npm install` without any user interaction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
